description:
Hello!

We are Fast Nauts. We are a group of computer science students who love technology, innovation, coding and space exploration. 

For the NASA Space Apps Challenge we are creating the Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer. This is an experience designed to help young explorers discover what it takes to be an astronaut. Through simulations mission challenges, resource management and creative problem-solving we aim to make space science engaging and easy to understand.
summary: We developed an interactive 3D interplanetary astronaut survival and exploration simulator that allows players to experience the challenges of establishing and maintaining space outposts on the Moon, Mars, Titan, and Europa. The project combines realistic planetary environments, astronaut and rover exploration, resource management, and engineering-based missions. Players must manage oxygen, water, food, fuel, electricity, spare parts, and crew health while responding to emergencies such as medical incidents, communication failures, equipment breakdowns, meteorite impacts, and planetary storms. Each planet features unique gravity, environmental conditions, hazards, and scientific discoveries. The simulator addresses the challenge by turning complex space engineering and survival problems into interactive, problem-solving experiences. It encourages players to think critically, make decisions, repair systems, manage limited resources, and understand how astronauts could survive in extreme environments. This project is important because it makes STEM learning engaging and practical while inspiring the next generation to explore space science, engineering, and planetary research.
